read: partial: abstract, Sections 1-2 (pp.1-5), evaluation setup, results, error analysis and discussion (pp.6-9); appendix skimmed by search
venue_now: arXiv preprint 2411.01492v2, 27 Feb 2025, headed 'Preprint' (p.1); the CVPR 2025 acceptance in the May entry is not shown in the text
what_it_is: EEE-Bench is a multimodal benchmark of 2,860 electrical and electronics engineering problems, each with an image such as a circuit, system diagram or plot, across ten subdomains (p.1-2, p.4). Problems were collected from official EEE exams and verified online sources, kept only when two distinct sources give identical solutions, and dropped if text-only GPT-4 answered them correctly in two trials; graduate students made two final quality checks (p.4). 72.0% are multiple-choice and the rest short free-form answers, nearly all numeric (p.4). Seventeen LLMs and LMMs are scored zero-shot on the final answer extracted by GPT-4o-mini; GPT-4o leads at 46.78% (p.1, p.7).
domain: engineering: electrical and electronics (10 subdomains: digital logic and microprocessor design, circuit theory and network analysis, analog circuits, power electronics and power systems, signals and systems, communication systems, control systems, electronic devices, electrical machines, electromagnetics); multimodal
size: 2,860 problems: 2,059 multiple-choice and 801 free-form (Table 1, p.4); 2,813 unique images (p.4); 17 models (p.1)
source_of_items: official EEE exams and verified online sources (p.4)
has_gold_traces: no (the released metadata lists question, image, answer, type and source, not solutions; p.4)
evaluation: final answer: multiple choice or free-form answers of at most one word, extracted by GPT-4o-mini and scored for accuracy; zero-shot, two runs averaged (p.4, p.7)
human_validation: two-source agreement filter on solutions and two final quality checks by graduate students (p.4); no validation of the answer extraction or scoring reported
contamination_measures: none reported (the text-only GPT-4 filter removes items solvable without the image, p.4; it is not presented as a contamination control)

engtrace_use.sentence: S-E1 (L182-190): [...] while specialized benchmarks like TransportBench, APBench, and EEE-Bench (Syed et al., 2024; Chen et al., 2025; Cheng et al., 2024; Li et al., 2025; Liu et al., 2025) are siloed within narrow sub-disciplines.
engtrace_use.explanation: EEE-Bench is confined to one discipline, electrical and electronics engineering (p.1), so 'siloed' fits; 'narrow sub-discipline' is loose, since it spans ten subdomains from digital logic to electromagnetics with 2,860 problems (p.2, p.4-5), more electrical subdomains than EngTrace's electrical branch has. The sentence also omits the features that set it apart in the comparison: every problem includes an image (p.4), 72.0% are multiple-choice (p.4), and scoring is final-answer accuracy after LLM answer extraction (p.7).

suggested_wording: EEE-Bench (Li et al., 2025) collects 2,860 image-based electrical and electronics engineering problems from exams and online sources, 72% of them multiple-choice and the rest short, mostly numeric answers, and scores only the extracted final answer.
facts_to_cite: 2,860 problems, 2,059 multiple-choice (72.0%) and 801 free-form (28.0%), all newly collected and all with images (Table 1, p.4)

Ten subdomains, e.g. circuit theory and network analysis (592), analog circuits (583), digital logic and microprocessor design (496), signals and systems (138), electromagnetics (102), communication systems (101) (p.4-5)

Collected from official EEE exams and verified online sources; kept only if two distinct sources give identical solutions; removed if text-only GPT-4 answered correctly twice; two final quality checks by graduate students (p.4)
Answers extracted by GPT-4o-mini and scored for accuracy; zero-shot, two runs averaged (p.7)
17 models; GPT-4o best at 46.78%, open-source best (InternVL2-26B) 26.89% (p.1, p.7)
Of GPT-4o's errors, 50.3% are reasoning errors and 26.5% image-perception errors (p.8)
Misleading captions lower GPT-4o's accuracy by 7.79% (p.3)
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: an engineering domain overlapping EngTrace's electrical branch (signals and systems, electromagnetics, communication systems; p.4-5); human quality checks of items (p.4); an error analysis separating reasoning from other errors (p.8). Lacks: generated instances (static, collected from exams and websites), gold traces (answers only, p.4), step-level evaluation (final answer after LLM extraction, p.7), validation of the evaluator, contamination measures. It is multimodal; EngTrace is text-only.
notes: The May entry adds 'Accepted to CVPR 2025'; the text file (arXiv v2, 27 Feb 2025) shows only 'Preprint', so the venue must be confirmed elsewhere. Who labelled GPT-4o's error types (p.8) is not stated. Grade: 'imprecise' rather than 'accurate' because the sentence's 'narrow sub-discipline' undersells a ten-subdomain, single-discipline benchmark and its multimodality is left out; 'accurate' is defensible if 'siloed' alone is read as the claim.
